collections.title: Kafka on the Shore
collections.creator: Haruki Murakami
collections.summary: A cross-media map of what the novel listens to, reads, invokes, and invents.
collections.scopeNote: Ten especially legible music moments are mapped here. The publisher's official playlist is the broader listening inventory; this smaller set does not pretend to be every passing artist or recording reference.
collections.textScopeNote: All 49 numbered chapters plus the Boy Named Crow framing sections in Philip Gabriel's English translation; book, play, poem, story, author-only, and in-novel library-title references are in scope. Music and film references are out of scope for this map.

nodes.title: Piano Sonata in D major, D 850
nodes.creator: Franz Schubert
nodes.role: Oshima uses the sonata's productive imperfection to describe how an interpreter can complete a work without erasing its form.

nodes.title: Sì, mi chiamano Mimì
nodes.creator: Giacomo Puccini · La bohème
nodes.role: The aria explains a cat's name and quietly characterizes the cultivated household around it.

nodes.title: Crossroads
nodes.creator: Cream
nodes.role: A literal song choice doubles as a structural signpost when Kafka reaches a decisive threshold.

nodes.title: Little Red Corvette
nodes.creator: Prince
nodes.role: Desire and unease arrive through the music rather than through explanatory narration.

nodes.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
nodes.creator: The Beatles
nodes.role: The record carries the teenage past of a person who is absent from the present but central to the novel's memory.

nodes.title: Sexy M.F.
nodes.creator: Prince and the New Power Generation
nodes.role: A blunt pop reference sits inside Kafka's unsettled exploration of adulthood and sexuality.

nodes.title: Piano Trio No. 7, “Archduke”
nodes.creator: Ludwig van Beethoven · Rubinstein, Heifetz, Feuermann recording
nodes.role: The trio becomes a catalyst for Hoshino's movement from detached listening toward attention and emotional connection.

nodes.title: Cello Concerto No. 1 in C major
nodes.creator: Joseph Haydn · Pierre Fournier recording
nodes.role: The concerto opens nostalgia and the possibility of change inside what had seemed like a fixed path.

nodes.title: Serenade No. 9 in D major, K. 320, “Posthorn”
nodes.creator: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
nodes.role: Its cheerful surface plays against a serious conversation, leaving the scene poised between reassurance and irony.

nodes.title: Kid A
nodes.creator: Radiohead
nodes.role: Kafka's repeated listening places him in a contemporary teenage world while the album's estrangement shadows the novel's atmosphere.

nodes.title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and a Night
nodes.creator: Traditional corpus; translated by Richard F. Burton
nodes.role: Kafka's chosen library reading; the old stories become a freer and more vivid reality than the anonymous station crowd.

nodes.title: The Sleeper and the Waker
nodes.creator: Traditional tale; translated by Richard F. Burton
nodes.role: Best source match for Gabriel's ‘Tale of Abu-l-Hasan, the Wag’; it locates the exact Burton volume behind Kafka's reading scene.

nodes.title: Symposium (also translated as The Banquet)
nodes.creator: Plato
nodes.role: Oshima uses Aristophanes' divided-human myth to talk about halves, solitude, sex, and the wish to become whole.

nodes.title: The Castle
nodes.creator: Franz Kafka
nodes.role: Part of Oshima's Kafka cluster: systems that stay legible enough to pursue but never fully yield.

nodes.title: The Trial
nodes.creator: Franz Kafka
nodes.role: One of the works that makes Kafka's chosen name a method, not merely a literary pose.

nodes.title: The Metamorphosis
nodes.creator: Franz Kafka
nodes.role: The familiar work in Oshima's cluster; it establishes transformation without explaining it away.

nodes.title: In the Penal Colony
nodes.creator: Franz Kafka
nodes.role: Kafka Tamura's favorite image is the punishment machine: law becomes literal inscription on the body.

nodes.title: Collected Works of Natsume Sōseki
nodes.creator: Natsume Sōseki
nodes.role: A library shelf and author-world that prepares the later close discussion of The Miner.

nodes.title: The Tale of Genji
nodes.creator: Murasaki Shikibu; modern-Japanese translation by Jun'ichirō Tanizaki
nodes.role: The living-spirit model lets intense attachment act at a distance; Kafka later begins the work rather than merely hearing about it.

nodes.title: The Miner
nodes.creator: Natsume Sōseki
nodes.role: Oshima treats it as an anti-bildungsroman: a disturbing experience need not deliver tidy growth or a moral certificate.

nodes.title: Poppies (The Poppy / Gubijinsō)
nodes.creator: Natsume Sōseki
nodes.role: One of the Sōseki works named around the contrast with The Miner.

nodes.title: Sanshirō
nodes.creator: Natsume Sōseki
nodes.role: Named as a more conventional formation novel against which The Miner can be read.

nodes.title: Kokoro
nodes.creator: Natsume Sōseki
nodes.role: A named Sōseki comparator in the chapter's discussion of character and development.

nodes.title: Goethe's ‘everything is a metaphor’ idea
nodes.creator: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
nodes.role: The author and idea are direct; scholars trace the line toward Faust Part II, but the novel does not safely name that title.

nodes.title: An unnamed book about Adolf Eichmann's trial
nodes.creator: Unidentified
nodes.role: A handwritten maxim inside the book turns imagination into responsibility; the novel does not identify the book's author or edition.

nodes.title: Responsibilities
nodes.creator: W. B. Yeats
nodes.role: The maxim found inside the Eichmann-trial book traces to the epigraph of Yeats's 1914 collection, where it is attributed to an ‘Old Play.’

nodes.title: Macbeth
nodes.creator: William Shakespeare
nodes.role: Johnnie Walker invokes the play while fate, imagination, and enacted violence collapse into one another.

nodes.title: Aeschylus (play title not stated with confidence)
nodes.creator: Aeschylus
nodes.role: Named in Oshima's Greek-tragedy discussion around Cassandra, knowledge, and powerlessness.

nodes.title: Euripides (play title not stated with confidence)
nodes.creator: Euripides
nodes.role: Named with Aeschylus as a route into Cassandra and the trap of foreknowledge without authority.

nodes.title: Romeo and Juliet
nodes.creator: William Shakespeare
nodes.role: A compact analogy inside the larger discussion of fate and tragic action.

nodes.title: An unspecified work by Leo Tolstoy
nodes.creator: Leo Tolstoy
nodes.role: Tolstoy is named, but the novel does not supply a work title secure enough for this map.

nodes.title: Electra
nodes.creator: Sophocles
nodes.role: Oshima has reread and quotes the play; inherited violence and obligation do not become clean merely because they are ancient.

nodes.title: The Hollow Men
nodes.creator: T. S. Eliot
nodes.role: Used against empty, unimaginative moral language: interior vacancy can still produce consequence.

nodes.title: Aristotle's tragedy and rhetoric concepts
nodes.creator: Aristotle
nodes.role: Aristotle is credited for ideas about metaphor and tragedy; Rhetoric and Poetics are sensible source works but their titles are not secure direct quotations here.

nodes.title: Oedipus Rex
nodes.creator: Sophocles
nodes.role: The novel's central fate structure: knowledge and virtue do not let Oedipus step outside the prophecy he is trying to defeat.

nodes.title: Ugetsu Monogatari (Tales of Moonlight and Rain)
nodes.creator: Ueda Akinari
nodes.role: A Japanese counterweight to Genji: spirits can be driven by loyalty and promise, not only erotic jealousy.

nodes.title: The Chrysanthemum Pledge
nodes.creator: Ueda Akinari
nodes.role: The specific Ugetsu story under discussion; a promise survives bodily limits and foreshadows the novel's memory/spirit logic.

nodes.title: Miss Saeki's unnamed book of lightning-strike interviews
nodes.creator: Miss Saeki (in-world author)
nodes.role: The plot-relevant interview book includes Kafka's father and intensifies Kafka's hypothesis about Miss Saeki.

nodes.title: Legends of Kagawa Prefecture
nodes.creator: Unidentified / possibly in-novel title
nodes.role: One of the local-library books Hoshino and Nakata use to turn place into a searchable trail.

nodes.title: Legends of Kōbō Daishi in Shikoku
nodes.creator: Unidentified / possibly in-novel title
nodes.role: A local legend book used during the practical search through Shikoku's memory.

nodes.title: A History of Takamatsu
nodes.creator: Unidentified / possibly in-novel title
nodes.role: Local history consulted as evidence rather than mystical interpretation.

nodes.title: Famous Stones of Japan
nodes.creator: Unidentified / possibly in-novel title
nodes.role: A deliberately literal research handle for the entrance stone.

nodes.title: Cats of the World
nodes.creator: Unidentified / possibly in-novel title
nodes.role: A comic and literal library choice that keeps Nakata's cat-world beside the larger metaphysical search.

nodes.title: Matter and Memory
nodes.creator: Henri Bergson
nodes.role: The philosophy student supplies a vocabulary for body and spirit, present and past, and memory as more than stored representation.

nodes.title: An unspecified work by G. W. F. Hegel
nodes.creator: G. W. F. Hegel
nodes.role: Hegel is quoted or paraphrased, but the novel does not name a secure title.

nodes.title: Chekhov's gun principle
nodes.creator: Anton Chekhov
nodes.role: The pistol principle is applied to the entrance stone: a conspicuous element creates an expectation that it will act.

nodes.title: Federico García Lorca (work not specified)
nodes.creator: Federico García Lorca
nodes.role: Named in the Spanish Civil War context rather than assigned a specific book.

nodes.title: Ernest Hemingway (work not specified)
nodes.creator: Ernest Hemingway
nodes.role: Named in the Spanish Civil War context; no specific title is made canonical here.

nodes.title: Charles Dickens (work not specified)
nodes.creator: Charles Dickens
nodes.role: A visual comparison for the buildings Nakata observes outside the Takamatsu hotel, not a reading assignment.

nodes.title: Aladdin
nodes.creator: Traditional tale transmitted through Antoine Galland's French Nights
nodes.role: An Arabian Nights allusion that extends the novel's bottle, wish, and released-force imagery.

nodes.title: The Frog Prince
nodes.creator: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm
nodes.role: A familiar fairy-tale comparison, not a recommendation to begin a Grimm sequence.

nodes.title: Rousseau's fence and civilization idea
nodes.creator: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
nodes.role: The idea about fences, ownership, and civilization is direct; the Discourse is likely provenance, not a securely named title.

nodes.title: An unnamed book about Napoleon's 1812 invasion of Russia
nodes.creator: Unidentified
nodes.role: A historical book is present, but neither author nor title is supplied.

nodes.title: Hansel and Gretel
nodes.creator: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm
nodes.role: A forest, abandonment, and homeward-path allusion inside the novel's own dangerous woods.

nodes.title: Beethoven and His Generation
nodes.creator: Unidentified / possibly in-novel title
nodes.role: Hoshino's library reading makes listening historical and relational rather than a vague ‘classical music’ upgrade.

nodes.title: Hector Berlioz's remark on encountering Hamlet
nodes.creator: Hector Berlioz
nodes.role: The quotation frames art as a before-and-after encounter for Hoshino; it is provenance for Hamlet, not another book title.

nodes.title: Hamlet
nodes.creator: William Shakespeare
nodes.role: Reached through Berlioz: one complete encounter enlarges Hoshino's inner world rather than merely giving him cultural facts.

nodes.title: ‘Kafka on the Shore’ song, lyrics, sheet music, LP, and painting
nodes.creator: Miss Saeki (in-world artifacts)
nodes.role: A single fictional artifact cluster binds text, music, image, memory, and the novel's title; it is not a real record or book to source externally.
